verification_report.summary: The proof is correct conditional on Inputs A, C, K, and V, which were treated as hypotheses rather than independently verified. Every deduction was checked in textual order. In the forward direction, b=1/(1-a) supplies the required competitor, and Input V applies in the scaled background a theta before passing to the limit a→1, proving equality of both volumes. In the converse, normalization by constants preserves masses and envelope nonemptiness. The explicit competitor phi-bj makes each q_j genuine; the defining inequality and canonical representatives give phi-bj<=q_j<=phi. Also phi-j<=u_j<=phi, so both q_j and u_j are equivalent to phi. Off the pluripolar poles, q_j is the envelope of b*u_j-(b-1)*phi. Contact support, positivity of the mixed products for s_j=q_j/b+(1-1/b)*phi, and equality-set comparison for s_j<=u_j give the claimed factor b^n. The condition j>k gives phi-j<-k on {u>-k}, so locality applies exactly where required. Under collapse, one first fixes k and takes j sufficiently large; only afterward does k tend to infinity. Pole negligibility then yields lower_vol(phi)<=b^n*(upper_vol(phi)-integral MA(u)). Constant translations of competitors transfer envelope emptiness to every u' equivalent to u; Input K forces the corresponding truncation envelopes to collapse as well. Taking the supremum of their target masses, equivalently the infimum of the resulting right-hand sides, yields lower_vol(phi)<=b^n*(upper_vol(phi)-upper_vol(u))=0, contradicting the assumed positive lower volume. No extremizing representative or uniform limit over all u' is required. Input K therefore gives genuine Q_b for every b>1, and b=1 is automatic. Both definitions coincide and both volumes agree with those of phi; no additional global positive volume hypothesis is used. The contextual attribution matches the full-volume specialization of [XL26, Lemma 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13446v1), but supplies no premise of this verification.
